_meta.description: Curated catalogue of documented high-impact flood / extreme-rain incidents in the four VARUNA AI regions.

fields.rainfall_mm: Representative peak accumulation (see rainfall_window_days) at the most affected gauge(s).
fields.deaths: Approximate reported deaths attributed to the event (state-level where noted).
fields.displaced: Approximate people in relief camps / displaced.
fields.causes: Normalised cause tags used for similarity matching.

_meta.disclaimer: Figures are rounded approximations compiled from public government situation reports and news coverage for demonstration. Verify against official NDMA / SDMA records before operational use.

incidents.name: Kerala floods (Great Flood of 2018)
incidents.summary: About 2.5x normal August rainfall fell on already saturated catchments; 35 of 54 reservoirs, including Idukki and Idamalayar, had to open their shutters. Periyar and Pamba overflowed and Chengannur, Aluva and Kuttanad stayed submerged for days.
incidents.source: Govt. of Kerala PDNA (2018); IMD rainfall report

incidents.name: Kerala floods & Puthumala / Kavalappara landslides
incidents.summary: An intense spell over Wayanad and Malappuram triggered the Puthumala (Meppadi) and Kavalappara landslides; the Chaliyar flooded Nilambur town.

incidents.name: Kerala October 2021 cloudburst (Koottickal / Kokkayar)
incidents.summary: A localised extreme rain spell caused flash floods and landslides at Koottickal and Kokkayar; the Manimala and Pamba rose sharply.

incidents.name: Wayanad landslides (Mundakkai-Chooralmala)
incidents.summary: About 570 mm in 48 hours on saturated slopes triggered debris flows that wiped out Mundakkai and Chooralmala in Meppadi panchayat.

incidents.name: Kerala monsoon floods 2013
incidents.summary: A vigorous monsoon onset flooded Kuttanad and the Vembanad lake fringe; backwater levels delayed drainage.

incidents.name: Mumbai 26 July deluge
incidents.summary: 944 mm fell at Santacruz in 24 hours. The Mithi river overflowed during high tide, storm drains built for 25 mm/h were overwhelmed, and the Saki Naka landslide followed. Over 1,000 deaths across Maharashtra.
incidents.source: Fact Finding Committee on Mumbai Floods (2006); IMD

incidents.name: Mumbai floods 29 August 2017
incidents.summary: About 330 mm in 12 hours coincided with a 3.3 m high tide. Hindmata, Sion and Andheri subway waterlogged, and suburban rail halted.

incidents.name: Mumbai floods & Malad wall collapse
incidents.summary: 375 mm in 24 hours; a retaining wall at Pimpripada, Malad East collapsed on hillside hutments. Widespread waterlogging at subways.

incidents.name: Chembur & Vikhroli landslides
incidents.summary: An overnight intense spell of 250 mm triggered landslides onto hillside settlements at Bharat Nagar (Chembur) and Surya Nagar (Vikhroli).

incidents.name: Mumbai waterlogging June 2014
incidents.summary: Moderate-heavy rain during a high tide over 4.5 m caused waterlogging in Hindmata, Sion and low-lying coastal koliwadas.

incidents.name: Chennai floods 2015 (Chembarambakkam release)
incidents.summary: After a month of rain saturated the soil, 490 mm fell at Tambaram on 1 December. A large Chembarambakkam release sent the Adyar into Mudichur, Manapakkam, Saidapet and Kotturpuram. Encroached lakes and marshes could not absorb the water.

incidents.name: Chennai November 2021 floods
incidents.summary: About 215 mm overnight, the highest November day since 2015, left T. Nagar, Pulianthope and Korattur waterlogged for days because of inadequate storm-water drains.

incidents.name: Cyclone Michaung floods
incidents.summary: Cyclone Michaung stalled offshore and dumped 400-440 mm over 36 hours on south Chennai. Storm surge and high tide blocked outfalls, and Velachery and Pallikaranai stayed inundated for several days.

incidents.name: Chennai floods October-December 2005
incidents.summary: Successive depressions brought over 400 mm. Surplus water from Chembarambakkam and Puzhal flooded the Adyar and Cooum banks.

incidents.name: Assam floods 2012
incidents.summary: The Brahmaputra and tributaries crossed danger marks across 27 districts and 4.8 million people were affected. Kaziranga was about 80% submerged with heavy wildlife losses.

incidents.name: Assam floods August 2017
incidents.summary: The second wave of the 2017 monsoon hit 3.3 million people. Releases from Bhutan's Kurichu dam swelled the Beki in Barpeta and several embankments breached.

incidents.name: Assam floods 2020
incidents.summary: Multiple waves from May to August affected about 5.7 million people. Kaziranga was about 90% submerged and Majuli was cut off repeatedly.

incidents.name: Assam floods & Silchar submergence 2022
incidents.summary: Record June rainfall. A breach at Bethukandi on the Barak left Silchar about 90% under water for over a week. Kopili releases and overflow flooded Hojai and Nagaon, and 8.9 million people were affected.

incidents.name: Ranganadi flash flood 2008
incidents.summary: A sudden release from the Ranganadi hydro project during heavy rain sent a flash flood into North Lakhimpur. This triggered a review of dam-release protocols.

incidents.name: Assam floods July 2024
incidents.summary: About 2.4 million people were affected in 29 districts. Dibrugarh town stayed waterlogged for over a week, and more than 150 animals died in Kaziranga.

incidents.name: Guwahati urban flash floods 2022
incidents.summary: Short-duration heavy rain flooded Anil Nagar and Nabin Nagar along the Bharalu. Hill-cutting runoff and choked drains caused chest-deep water in minutes.
